content.thinking: I'm leaning toward state-divergence as the failure mode, since the cache is just a copy and the purchase ledger checks out. The likely subject is io-summary-cache. It isn't an internal dependency failure, though the cache is internal and owned by checkout-platform, and state-divergence still fits best.

hypotheses.subject: io-summary-cache
hypotheses.summary: The cached spend totals (io-summary-cache) stopped keeping up with the purchase ledger from 2026-11-07T13:08:00Z and began being served stale at 2026-11-07T16:01:08Z. The ledger is right and only the derived copy is behind. No deploy, config change or rollout is recorded.

supporting_evidence.claim: 90 of 240 cached spend figures disagree with the purchases behind them. The purchases are correct and the cached copies are behind; the oldest unaccounted purchase was recorded at 2026-11-07T13:08:00Z.
get_changes: nothing changed in the window; the deployment has converged on 3 replicas with no deployment in the history; all pods run on identical V100 nodes that started at 2026-11-07T04:06:08Z.

hypotheses.subject: io-summary-cache
hypotheses.summary: The internal cache service io-summary-cache, owned by checkout-platform, is failing to apply updates and so serves stale spend figures.

supporting_evidence.claim: The service register lists io-summary-cache as internal; it holds the spend figure copies that are stale.
